name: Free-play tissue bed
description: Full-thickness bed: skin, subcutaneous fat with septa and perforators, Scarpa's fascia, deep fascia, muscle. A small subcutaneous lipoma sits off-centre. No procedure; learn what each setting does to each layer.

education.goal: Explore how each FT10 mode and power setting affects skin, fat, fascia and muscle. Make a clean 3 cm incision through dermis with a thermal rim under 0.5 mm, then control any bleeder you expose.

success.label: Less than 5 mm3 of carbonized tissue

failurePoints.consequence: Carbonized eschar: insulating, delays healing, hides deeper injury.
failurePoints.teaching: Char means the tissue has desiccated and current can no longer do useful work. Lift off earlier; use short taps.

failurePoints.consequence: Skin edge necrosis: wound dehiscence and a wide scar.
failurePoints.teaching: Cut mode at a steady pace keeps the thermal rim under half a millimetre. Slowing down or using coag on the edge widens it.

failurePoints.consequence: Char plug over an open lumen rebleeds once the patient's blood pressure rises: hematoma.
failurePoints.teaching: Grasp the vessel with forceps first and buzz the forceps so the walls are apposed when they coagulate.

decisionPoints.prompt: You have reached the deep fascia. Stay above it or go through?

options.label: Go through
options.outcome: Enters muscle; expect bleeding and twitching.

ambiguity.description: Fat thickness varies +-15 % so the fascia depth is not known in advance.
Perforator positions are seeded per attempt.
